hook.line: Every plan has one thing somebody forgot: the budget, the traffic, the neighbour who complains. When you want to put that thing on the table, this is the phrase.
hook.es: Hay que tener en cuenta que el presupuesto es limitado.
hook.en: We have to bear in mind that the budget is limited.

examples.es: Hay que tener en cuenta que el presupuesto es limitado.
examples.en: We have to bear in mind that the budget is limited.

examples.es: Hay que tener en cuenta el tráfico.
examples.en: You have to take the traffic into account.

examples.es: Hay que tener en cuenta que Vale no trabaja los lunes.
examples.en: We have to bear in mind that Vale doesn't work on Mondays.

examples.es: Hay que tener en cuenta que la fuente es anónima.
examples.en: We have to bear in mind that the source is anonymous.

examples.es: No hay que tener en cuenta los rumores.
examples.en: We shouldn't take the rumours into account.
What do we have to bear in mind?

rule:
*Hay que tener en cuenta* flags something that must weigh on the decision. It is not an aside: it is a real limit on the conclusion.

After it comes either a thing or a full sentence with *que*: *hay que tener en cuenta el tráfico*, *hay que tener en cuenta que el presupuesto es limitado*. The verb after *que* is in the ordinary indicative.

*Hay que* has no subject, like English "one has to". Add *no* in front and it means "we shouldn't": *no hay que tener en cuenta los rumores*.
smallPrint: Teachers call *hay que* an impersonal obligation. The frame is neutral to formal, so it suits reports and meetings.

readAndPick.es: Hay que tener en cuenta el tráfico.
options: We have to take the traffic into account.
We took the traffic into account.
We don't have to think about traffic.

readAndPick.es: No hay que tener en cuenta los rumores.
options: We have to take the rumours into account.
We shouldn't take the rumours into account.
We took the rumours into account.

readAndPick.es: Hay que tener en cuenta que la fuente es anónima.
options: We have to bear in mind that the source is anonymous.
We have to find an anonymous source.
We forgot that the source is anonymous.
We have to consider traffic.
We will consider traffic.
We took traffic into account.

readAndPick.es: Tengo que tener en cuenta la hora.
options: One has to consider the time.
I have to consider the time.
We have to consider the time.
What did we consider?
What do we have to bear in mind?
Who has to bear it in mind?

readAndPick.es: Habrá que tener en cuenta la lluvia.
options: We will have to take the rain into account.
We had to take the rain into account.
We don't need to think about rain.

readAndPick.es: Hubo que tener en cuenta que era tarde.
options: We have to remember it is late.
We had to bear in mind that it was late.
We will have to remember it is late.

readAndPick.es: No tuvieron en cuenta el precio.
options: They didn't take the price into account.
They don't have to consider the price.
We didn't take the price into account.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick the right words and type the whole sentence: *Hay que tener ___ el tráfico.* (*en cuenta* or *a cuenta*)
yourTurn.answer: Hay que tener en cuenta el tráfico.
yourTurn.why: The fixed phrase is *tener en cuenta*, "to take into account".

yourTurn.prompt: Pick the right words and type the whole sentence: *Hay que tener en cuenta ___ presupuesto es limitado.* (*el* or *que el*)
yourTurn.answer: Hay que tener en cuenta que el presupuesto es limitado.
yourTurn.why: A full sentence needs *que* in front of it; a plain thing does not.

yourTurn.prompt: Type it in Spanish: We have to bear in mind that Vale doesn't work on Mondays.
yourTurn.answer: Hay que tener en cuenta que Vale no trabaja los lunes.
yourTurn.why: *Hay que tener en cuenta que* plus an ordinary sentence in the indicative.

yourTurn.prompt: Type it in Spanish: You have to take the traffic into account.
yourTurn.answer: Hay que tener en cuenta el tráfico.
yourTurn.why: A thing follows directly, with no *que*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type it in Spanish: What do we have to bear in mind?
yourTurn.why: The question word goes first and the phrase stays the same.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it negative: *Hay que tener en cuenta los rumores.*
yourTurn.answer: No hay que tener en cuenta los rumores.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it about the past (we had to): *Hay que tener en cuenta la hora.*
yourTurn.answer: Hubo que tener en cuenta la hora.
yourTurn.why: *Hay que* moves to *hubo que* for a single moment in the past.

pitfalls.wrong: Hay que tener en cuenta que el tráfico.
pitfalls.right: Hay que tener en cuenta el tráfico.
pitfalls.why: Almost. *Que* introduces a full sentence with its own verb; for just a noun, leave it out.

pitfalls.wrong: Hay que tener en cuenta de que el presupuesto es limitado.
pitfalls.right: Hay que tener en cuenta que el presupuesto es limitado.
pitfalls.why: Spanish says *tener en cuenta que*, with no *de* in the middle.

pitfalls.wrong: Hay que tener cuenta el tráfico.
pitfalls.right: Hay que tener en cuenta el tráfico.
pitfalls.why: The fixed phrase needs the *en*: *tener en cuenta*.

personal: Say one true thing someone has to bear in mind about you or your week, starting with *Hay que tener en cuenta que…*.
